name: צִיּוֹן
summary: Zion is the stronghold David captured and called the City of David, and in the psalms and prophets Yahweh’s holy mountain and city, Jerusalem, where he installed his king; the daughter of Zion is its people, called to rejoice at her king’s coming. The text gives no derivation of the name.

evidence.note: The stronghold of Zion is the City of David, where David takes up residence.
Yahweh has installed his king on Zion, his holy mountain.
The daughter of Zion is called to rejoice at the approach of her king.
John quotes the address when Jesus enters Jerusalem.
Greek Σιών, the name borrowed from Hebrew.

note: Moved from the former word entry `9iyywon`, whose three senses (the stronghold taken by David; Yahweh’s holy mountain and city; Zion addressed as its people) are folded into the summary and evidence. TIPNR files Zion under Jerusalem@Gen.14.18. The name was entered under its own consonants (ציונ). Its location is fixed by 2 Samuel 5, but neither that narrative nor the Psalms derive it from צִיָּה “dryness.” Proposed derivations from a fortress or landmark remain uncertain.
